REC-0023.title: Mass graves found in Uvira (Kavimvira and Kilomoni, 27 to 28 February 2026)
REC-0023.actor_line: AFC/M23 supported by the RDF, per the South Kivu provincial government; perpetrators not attributed by the national government and BBC Gahuza
REC-0023.place_text: Kavimvira cemetery and road, Kilomoni quarter, Uvira city

counterclaims.text: AFC/M23's spokesperson told Reuters he knew of no mass graves during the group's time in Uvira and accused the DRC government of propaganda.

Rwanda's Ministry of Defence website answered the South Kivu governor's accusation that Rwanda and AFC/M23 were behind the Uvira massacres by saying the city had been in chaos since the AFC/M23 withdrawal, with killings, looting and sexual violence.

Rwanda's Office of the Government Spokesperson said the HRW report nowhere attributes the mass graves to Rwanda and documents summary executions and sexual violence by the FARDC and Wazalendo before and during their withdrawal from Uvira.

notes: BBC Gahuza reported two mass graves holding 31 and 141 bodies, whereas Actualite.cd reported 121 civilians buried at the Kavinvira cemetery and 30 in Kilomoni.{{c:r1-ST-M23-2026-013,r1-UV-2026Q1-041}}
The Council of Ministers heard of a grave near the World Food Programme office reportedly holding about 35 bodies.{{c:r1-UV-2026Q1-040}}
The governor later spoke of up to 49 mass graves identified in the Uvira sector, with more than 241 bodies counted in three of them.{{c:r1-UV-2026Q3-022}}
Foxtime.cd reported, on an undated page, that the governor announced at least 344 bodies in three mass graves in Uvira and its outskirts.{{c:r9-V-FU-007}}

Opinion Info and Actualite.cd reported that the governor said on 2 April 2026 that about 210 bodies had been found in three mass graves, named by Opinion Info as Kamvivira, Kilomoni and Kimanga.{{c:r9-V-UV2-004}}
The two totals attributed to the same governor differ (344 and about 210), and both differ from the February counts recorded above.{{c:r9-V-FU-007,r9-V-UV2-004}}

REC-0250.title: Casualties reported from the fighting for Goma (Goma, 23 January to 7 February 2025)
REC-0250.actor_line: Fighting between M23 and FARDC and allies, as described by the sources; no party named for the deaths

counterclaims.text: Bertrand Bisimwa publicly denied civilian deaths in the fighting for Goma, claiming that all fatalities were combatants.

BBC Gahuza reported that M23 said the more than 2,500 people who died in the recent fighting in Goma were government soldiers (FARDC) and Wazalendo; that Bertrand Bisimwa, one of the leaders of M23, said no family in Goma was in mourning because of those dead; and that he said the bodies removed from the streets and buried were those of FARDC soldiers and their collaborators, including Wazalendo, FDLR, European mercenaries and Burundian forces, who died in battle.

BBC Gahuza reported that Patrick Muyaya, spokesperson of the Kinshasa government, had recently said that more than 2,000 bodies were still in the streets of Goma needing burial, and that he accused Rwandan forces and M23 of killing civilians in the recent fighting in Goma and its surroundings.
AFC/M23 secretary Kimbulungu said AFC/M23 found 874 bodies in Goma from 2 to 13 February, while the Congolese government says about 3000 died, according to Umunota.

notes: The sources give different death figures for the fighting in Goma: BBC News Afrique reported that the UN said at least 2,900 people were killed, BBC News reported at least 700 killed, WHO reported 843 dead from 31 health facilities since 26 January, and Studio Hirondelle reported that the Health Minister had been told of more than 2,000 bodies to bury.{{c:r1-NKS-2025Q1-013,r1-NKS-2025Q1-014,r1-HC-2025-005,r1-NKS-2025Q1-012}}
The Group of Experts reported that the claims by Bertrand Bisimwa that all fatalities were combatants were contradicted by consistent reports of civilian casualties.{{c:r1-GOE-068}}

Umunota reported that AFC/M23 secretary Kimbulungu said AFC/M23 found 874 bodies in Goma from 2 to 13 February, while DW Kiswahili wrote that, according to the United Nations, about 3,000 people died.{{c:r7-L-M23-005,r7-L-M23-011}}

REC-0264.place_text: Rumangabo and Tshanzu, Rutshuru territory; Goma; Bukavu

counterclaims.text: The Office of the Government Spokesperson of Rwanda rejected Human Rights Watch's allegations of RDF involvement in forced recruitment, detention, torture, executions, forced labor or child recruitment, and rejected the collapsing of M23 and RDF into one actor.

Rwandan Government Spokesperson Yolande Makolo said, in reaction to a Human Rights Watch report, that 'the RDF is not AFC/M23' and that any proper investigation requires impartiality, access to where events happen, solid evidence, respect for the law and not announcing conclusions in advance or putting calls for sanctions first, according to Igihe.

Igihe reported that Government Spokesperson Yolande Makolo, in a post on X, dismissed the Human Rights Watch report as part of a 30-year pattern of anonymous claims, no site visits or forensics, and 'sanctions first and investigation later'.

Igihe reported that the Office of the Government Spokesperson of Rwanda said that no HRW investigator set foot at the places named in the report, and that there were no visits, no exhumations for investigation and no laboratory tests.

According to Igihe, the Rwandan government said HRW claims to have satellite images showing killings 'carried out by Rwandan forces and M23', with features resembling graves, but that HRW cannot confirm whether they are graves or other objects.

REC-0275.title: Mass escape from Munzenze prison, rapes of women prisoners and fire in the women's wing (Goma, 27 January 2025)
REC-0275.actor_line: Male inmates, per OHCHR fact-finding mission, UN News and the BBC; M23 role alleged by the Kinshasa side and denied by AFC/M23; perpetrators not identified in some accounts

counterclaims.text: Délion Kimbulungu, secretary of AFC/M23, presenting a report of AFC/M23, said the events at Munzenze prison happened in the morning while M23 arrived in the evening, and that their investigation found the prison escape had begun a few days before M23 arrived.
The Kinshasa side said the M23 group had a role in what it called the horror at Munzenze prison.
The New Times reported that Bisimwa said in an earlier, undated post that accusations against AFC-M23 are false and that the mass rapes of female prisoners occurred before AFC-M23's presence in Goma.
AFC/M23 secretary Kimbulungu said the escape of Munzenze inmates and the deaths of the women there happened before AFC/M23 fighters arrived, according to Umunota.

notes: Sources give different figures for the women held and killed at Munzenze prison: the BBC reported, citing an internal UN document, that between 165 and 167 women were assaulted by male inmates, the OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that most of the 160 women inmates died, and the BBC reported that 132 female prisoners and at least 25 children burned to death according to two sources.{{c:r1-SV-2025-001,r2-G-DOC-HRC-038,r1-SV-NK-2025-011}}

Accounts of who raped the women differ: the OHCHR fact-finding mission reported male inmates, Belga reported that it was not yet known whether the rapists were escaped prisoners, M23 rebels or members of other local militias, and the BBC reported that all sides were eager to blame someone else.{{c:r2-G-DOC-HRC-038,r1-NKS-2025Q1-016,r1-SV-NK-2025-012}}

The sources give different accounts of the toll: police investigator Robert Kayembe told DPA that over 160 women were raped and a number not yet established were burned, while DRC Foreign Minister Kayikwamba Wagner told the UN Security Council that 500 charred corpses were found in the prison.{{c:r3-G-RESP-002,r3-G-RESP-003}}

REC-0286.title: Armed raids on Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals and reported abduction of patients (Goma, 28 February to 3 March 2025)
REC-0286.actor_line: M23 fighters, per UN Human Rights Office, Amnesty International and the Group of Experts
REC-0286.place_text: Heal Africa hospital and CBCA Ndosho hospital, Goma
REC-0286.place: Heal Africa hospital and CBCA Ndosho hospital

counterclaims.text: An official AFC/M23 communiqué of 5 March 2025, signed by Lawrence Kanyuka, denied responsibility for the raids on Goma hospitals and acknowledged that 130 FARDC elements were taken, claiming the operation was peaceful because the elements had infiltrated the medical facilities.
Lawrence Kanyuka, political spokesperson of AFC/M23, said the UN statement was false because those arrested in the hospitals were FARDC soldiers who had gone there to hide.

The EastAfrican reported that the AFC strongly denies the UN human rights office's allegations of attacks on hospitals, saying its raid was aimed at securing medical infrastructure it said had been infiltrated by fighters.

Sultani Makenga, M23's military chief, said in an interview that Congolese army members in hospitals posed as patients or carers, that M23 found 14 weapons in hospitals and that hospital staff alerted them.

In an interview excerpt published on X on 13 March 2025, General Sultani Makenga, asked about the raid on the Heal Africa hospital, repeated that the men arrested were former FARDC pretending to be patients or hospital staff.

Bertrand Bisimwa, Lawrence Kanyuka and General Makenga issued public denials of responsibility, claiming an aim of securing hospitals from infiltrated rogue combatants, while the Group of Experts wrote that witnesses confirmed no weapons were found in the hospitals.

A DRC Interior Ministry communiqué of 6 March, as reported by Ouragan.cd, said the Rwandan army and its M23 auxiliaries took about a hundred patients and carers from Goma hospitals, among them Congolese soldiers, and that they were summarily executed.

notes: The sources give different dates and numbers for the hospital raids: Reuters reported that the UN Human Rights Office said M23 fighters raided CBCA Ndosho and Heal Africa hospitals on the night of 28 February taking 116 and 15 patients, Amnesty International said more than 130 people were abducted on the night of 28 February and the morning of 3 March, and the Group of Experts reported raids on 1 and 3 March in which 164 patients were abducted, 48 from Heal Africa and 116 from CBCA Ndosho.{{c:r1-HC-2025-001,r1-NKS-2025Q1-020,r1-GOE-055}}
Ouragan.cd's account of the Interior Ministry communiqué places the incursions into the Ndosho and CBCA Virunga hospitals on 28 February and on 3 and 4 March.{{c:r7-L-DRC-003}}

REC-0345.title: Alleged summary executions of hundreds of civilians by M23 in Binza (Rutshuru territory, July 2025)
REC-0345.actor_line: M23 and AFC/M23, with RDF alleged, per OHCHR, UN Group of Experts and Human Rights Watch
REC-0345.place_text: Binza groupement, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory (Nyamilima, Kisharo, Burambo, Kiseguro, Katwiguro, Musinga, Kigarigari)

counterclaims.text: AFC deputy coordinator Bertrand Bisimwa, at a press conference in Goma on 7 August 2025, called the UN report on the alleged massacre of more than 300 civilians in Rutshuru in July non factuel, saying the villages named as massacre sites would lie in the protected zone of Virunga National Park and therefore be uninhabited.

The Government of Rwanda said in a statement that it rejects the false accusations in the recent OHCHR statement, which alleges without any evidence that the Rwanda Defence Force aided in the killing of 319 civilians in farms in eastern DRC.

The Government of Rwanda said in a statement that it firmly rejects the findings of Human Rights Watch, OHCHR and UNJHRO alleging mass killing of civilians in Binza, and that Human Rights Watch itself admits that it did not independently verify the alleged killings.

BBC Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 said the new Human Rights Watch report accusing it of killing at least 140 civilians, mostly Hutu, is 'a lie' with 'no foundation'; in a statement by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka it said the HRW and UN allegations are politically motivated, and that HRW deliberately avoided mentioning armed groups it says work with Kinshasa, including FDLR, Nyatura, PARECO and Wazalendo.
AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the HRW and UN allegations were politically motivated and biased toward the DRC government, according to Kigali Today.

AFC/M23 called the Human Rights Watch report of at least 140 civilians killed a lie and distortion of the truth, said it had rejected the allegations on 7 August, and called the HRW and UN allegations politically motivated (per BBC Gahuza).
The Rwandan government said the RDF has nothing to do with the killings alleged by Human Rights Watch and that M23 is not controlled by Rwanda (per BBC Gahuza).

notes: Sources give different figures and dates for the July killings: the Group of Experts reported over 300 civilian casualties between 9 and 27 July, OHCHR said at least 319 civilians were killed between 9 and 21 July, the OHCHR fact-finding mission said hundreds of civilians were allegedly executed between 8 and 29 July, and Human Rights Watch reported executions between 10 and 30 July.{{c:r1-GOE-086,r1-NKS-2025Q3-003,r2-G-DOC-HRC-003,r1-NKS-2025Q3-001}}

MSF reported that 124 intentionally wounded people were treated at Rutshuru general referral hospital in July and August and that all survivors name armed men as the perpetrators, some citing the M23 armed group.{{c:r1-HC-NK-2025-010}}

REC-1008.title: Limited AFC/M23 and RDF pull-back from positions in Lubero territory (from 23 March 2026)
REC-1008.actor_line: RDF and AFC/M23, per the Group of Experts and Anadolu Agency
REC-1008.place_text: Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi, Kipese; Alimbongo, Kirumba, Kanyabayonga; Lubero territory

counterclaims.text: The North Kivu governor said he had observed an effective withdrawal from several areas and that the rebel movement was part of the implementation of the peace agreements.

According to Igihe, North Kivu Governor Erasto Bahati (AFC/M23 administration) dismissed the reports of withdrawal in a statement, saying the activities along the front were regular troop rotations within AFC/M23 and that the rumours were fuelled by social media and the Kinshasa government.

Igihe reported that AFC/M23 denied reports that it had begun withdrawing fighters from some areas it controls in the east of the country; in a communiqué, Erasto Bahati, whom Igihe calls the provincial governor, said what was happening on the front lines was a routine replacement of troops in the AFC/M23 military and that the reports were rumours fuelled by the Kinshasa authorities' social media.
A statement by Erasto Bahati, the AFC/M23-appointed North Kivu governor, dismissed reports of a pull-back and called the movements regular troop rotations (per Into Rwanda).

notes: The Group of Experts reported that the withdrawals began on 23 March 2026 but barely exceeded 15 to 20 km and amounted to tactical repositioning.{{c:r1-GOE-017}}
Anadolu Agency reported that the governor observed an effective withdrawal from several areas.{{c:r1-NKN-2026H1-003}}

Bwiza, citing information from inside AFC/M23, reported that the group decided to pull out of areas of Lubero as a confidence-building measure, while a statement by Erasto Bahati dismissed reports of a pull-back as routine troop rotation. {{c:r7-S2-M23A-022,r7-S2-M23B-016}}
